Chapter 3: System Analysis

3.1 Existing System

In many corporate, academic, and small-to-medium enterprise IT environments, the administration of physical assets, software entitlements, and technical helpdesk incidents is handled using disjointed, manual mechanisms. Physical equipment is tracked in decentralized desktop spreadsheets (e.g. Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets), software license keys are recorded on local text files or paper invoices, and support requests arrive haphazardly via email, instant messaging apps, or oral walk-ins.

This conventional approach lacks automated synchronization, concurrency controls, and tamper-proof verification, resulting in severe operational vulnerabilities across the organization as detailed in Table 3.1:

Table 3.1: Operational Deficiencies of the Existing Manual System
Manual System Practice Operational Deficiency & Institutional Risk
Unsynchronized Spreadsheets Multiple administrators edit separate file copies, causing conflicting records, duplicate entries, and "ghost" inventory items.
Untracked Handover Forms Paper issue slips get misplaced, leaving the organization with no legal proof of custody when an employee departs.
Manual License Key Tracking Keys are exposed in plain text; administrators miss renewal dates, causing unexpected service disruptions or compliance fines.
Ad-Hoc Email Support Queues Support requests lack priority classification and SLA tracking; critical hardware faults languish unassigned in personal inboxes.
Absence of Immutable Audit Trails Modifications, status alterations, and record deletions occur without historical logs, preventing accountability.
Manual Status Reconciliations Preparing compliance audit reports requires labor-intensive physical inventory checks, wasting valuable IT engineering hours.

3.2 Need for New System

To overcome the systemic liabilities of manual recordkeeping, an integrated software solution is mandatory. The core drivers compelling this development are:

  1. Unified Single Source of Truth: Eliminate fragmented spreadsheets by establishing a centralized, relational database storing all hardware, software, and ticket entities.
  2. Definitive Custody Tracking: Bind every physical device directly to a verified employee profile with atomic assignment locks to prevent inventory leakage.
  3. Vendor Compliance & Expiry Prevention: Enforce strict seat quotas and deliver automated alerts 30 days prior to license expiration dates.
  4. Measurable Service Level Agreements (SLAs): Formalize support resolution with priority-driven resolution windows and transparent state tracking.
  5. Regulatory Accountability: Ensure every system action is permanently preserved in an append-only, tamper-proof security audit log.

3.3 Software Requirements Specification (SRS)

3.3.1 Purpose, Scope & Definitions

This specification documents the functional and non-functional requirements for the AssetDesk system in conformance with the IEEE-830 standard. Key terminology used throughout this document is defined in Table 3.2:

Table 3.2: Engineering Abbreviations & Technical Definitions
Term Full Form Operational Definition
SRS Software Requirements Specification Formal IEEE-830 specification document defining complete system behavior.
RBAC Role-Based Access Control Authorization paradigm restricting resource access based on assigned user roles.
JWT JSON Web Token Stateless, cryptographically signed token used for secure API authentication.
CRUD Create, Read, Update, Delete Four foundational persistent storage operations executed across database entities.
REST Representational State Transfer Architectural style for network-based web services communicating over HTTP.
API Application Programming Interface Standardized interface exposing backend business logic to client consumers.
SLA Service Level Agreement Committed time threshold within which a reported issue must be resolved.
CSV Comma-Separated Values Plain-text tabular data format widely used for accounting and spreadsheet interchange.
SPA Single Page Application Web app that dynamically rewrites the current web page without full browser reloads.
SMTP Simple Mail Transfer Protocol Standard protocol used by background workers to dispatch alert notifications.

3.3.2 Overall System Description & User Classes

User Persona Assigned Role Key System Responsibilities & Entitlements
System Administrator ADMIN Full governance: user creation, asset CRUD, license management, audit review, CSV exports.
Support Technician IT_SUPPORT Operational desk: asset assignments, status updates, ticket triage, comments, and resolution.
Standard Employee EMPLOYEE Self-service: view assigned hardware/licenses, submit support tickets, track ticket status.

3.3.3 Functional Requirements Specification (Part 1: FR-01 to FR-10)

The system functions are formally partitioned into discrete requirements. Each functional requirement is mapped to its parent module, priority level, and the verified automated integration/system test ID confirming implementation:

Table 3.3: Functional Requirements Matrix (FR-01 to FR-10)
Req ID Functional Requirement Description Module Priority Verified By Test ID
FR-01 User Login: Authenticate users via email and bcrypt-hashed password; issue 24-hour cryptographically signed JWT. M1 Must IT-M1-01, ST-01
FR-02 Role-Based Access: Restrict endpoint execution strictly according to user role (ADMIN, IT_SUPPORT, EMPLOYEE). M1 Must IT-M1-12, SEC-02
FR-03 User Management: Enable ADMIN to register new staff members, update role assignments, and deactivate user accounts. M1 Must IT-M1-18, ST-13
FR-04 Password Modification: Allow authenticated users to change passwords upon verifying current password hash. M1 Must IT-M1-25, SEC-05
FR-05 Asset Registration: Register physical assets with unique asset tag, serial, model, category, purchase date, and specs. M2 Must IT-M2-01, ST-04
FR-06 Asset Record Update: Allow authorized staff to update hardware details, specifications, warranty, and location. M2 Should IT-M2-10, ST-05
FR-07 Asset Assignment: Concurrency-safe atomic assignment and unassignment of hardware items to employees. M2 Must IT-M2-16, ST-06
FR-08 Asset Lifecycle Transitions: Enforce valid status transitions between IN_USE, AVAILABLE, IN_REPAIR, and RETIRED. M2 Must IT-M2-24, ST-07
FR-09 Asset Search & Filters: Enable multi-criteria filtering by category, status, assignment state, and search terms. M2 Should IT-M2-31, ST-03
FR-10 Software License Management: Catalog enterprise software with purchased seats, vendor, and license keys. M3 Must IT-M3-01, ST-08
Traceability Guarantee: Every functional requirement is bound to executable integration test suites, guaranteeing zero unimplemented specifications in the codebase.

3.3.3 Functional Requirements Specification (Part 2: FR-11 to FR-20)

Continued specification matrix detailing software seat quotas, support ticket lifecycle, immutable logging, and administrative intelligence:

Table 3.4: Functional Requirements Matrix (FR-11 to FR-20)
Req ID Functional Requirement Description Module Priority Verified By Test ID
FR-11 Seat Allocation & Deallocation: Allocate licenses to users while blocking allocations when purchased seats are exhausted. M3 Must IT-M3-14, ST-09
FR-12 License Expiry Warnings: Automatically flag licenses nearing expiration (≤30 days) via scheduled node-cron service. M3 Must IT-M3-26, UT-M3-07
FR-13 Ticket Submission: Allow employees to create support tickets with title, description, category, and priority level. M4 Must IT-M4-01, ST-11
FR-14 Ticket Assignment: Assign unassigned support tickets to designated IT support technicians with audit logging. M4 Should IT-M4-15, ST-12
FR-15 Ticket State Machine: Enforce strict linear status transitions: OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED → CLOSED. M4 Must IT-M4-22, ST-10
FR-16 Ticket Communication: Enable threaded conversation comments between ticket creator and assigned support engineer. M4 Should IT-M4-33, UT-M4-09
FR-17 Security Audit Logging: Record immutable event logs containing timestamp, action, actor ID, target entity, and IP address. M5 Must IT-M5-01, SEC-04
FR-18 Dashboard KPI Summaries: Aggregate real-time statistics (total assets, active tickets, license seats, expiring alerts). M5 Should IT-M5-12, ST-02
FR-19 CSV Report Generation: Export compliant CSV files for assets, licenses, tickets, and audit trails with custom filters. M5 Should IT-M5-22, ST-15
FR-20 License Key Masking: Mask sensitive software license keys (XXXX-****-****-XXXX) for standard users. M3 Must IT-M3-08, SEC-09
Verification Integrity: Functional correctness for all 20 requirements is backed by 272 automated test cases executed across isolated memory databases.

3.3.4 Non-Functional Requirements (NFR)

System quality attributes were measured quantitatively against verified benchmark logs and automated testing results:

Table 3.5: Non-Functional Requirements & Verified Engineering Metrics
Quality Attribute Measurable Engineering Target Real Measured Verification Result
Security Encrypted passwords (bcrypt 10 rounds), signed JWT tokens, role guards, Helmet HTTP security headers, injection defense. 12/12 dedicated security tests passed (SEC-01..12). XSS sanitization & NoSQL injection verified.
Performance Query endpoint p95 latency under 100ms; login response time under 250ms for 50 concurrent requests. Measured: POST /auth/login avg 75.82ms; GET /assets avg 7.49ms; GET /tickets avg 7.96ms (50 samples).
Usability Responsive layout on 1366×768 and 1920×1080 screens; clear validation errors; actionable empty/loading states. 16/16 Playwright system journeys (ST-01..16) validated with automated UI screenshots.
Reliability Zero server crashes during malformed input payloads; robust Express exception handler returns uniform JSON error payloads. 100% test pass rate (272/272 tests passing) with 87.16% statement coverage and 0 unhandled rejections.
Maintainability Modular directory architecture, strict separation of concerns (MVC), unified constants, ESLint zero errors. 19,383 lines of clean, self-documenting JavaScript adhering to Prettier and ESLint standards.
Portability Run on Linux/macOS/Windows servers via Node.js runtime; client compatible with all modern evergreen browsers. Verified on Node.js 20/24 LTS across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit rendering engines.
